report.summary: The change makes the native merge gate (RepositoryCiDO.mergeBlock) count a required job with conclusion `skipped` as passed. The spec (10 Project CI, Merge gate) says every required job must be `success`. In this DO, a job ends `skipped` exactly when one of its `needs` ended without success (pump(), line 531-532). So if a required job's dependency fails, is cancelled or times out, the gate opens and the PR can merge. That is fail-open on a security-relevant guard. There is no spec change in the same diff (CLAUDE.md rule 16) and no test for the new behavior.

findings.text: The merge gate now treats a skipped required job as passed. Skipped means a dependency did not succeed, so failed builds can merge. The spec requires every required job to be `success`.

evidence.why: pump() marks a queued job skipped when any need finished without success: `if (needs.some((need) => need?.status === "completed" && need.conclusion !== "success")) { this.completeJob(job, "skipped", ...` (lines 531-532). Failing case: the pipeline has required: ["test"] and test needs build, and build is not required. When build fails, test is completed/skipped, mergeBlock returns null, and the merge goes ahead even though nothing passed. The spec line in docs/10 Project CI.md says: "a native merge needs the newest run for the exact head SHA and the current revision, with every `required` job `success`." CLOUDFLARE-CODE-HOSTING-PLAN.md also says incomplete results "cannot grant merge permission".

findings.text: The behavior change has no matching spec edit. CLAUDE.md rule 16 asks for one in the same change, and rule 14 asks for a test; the diff touches only this one line, and apps/tempo/test/worker/project-ci.cases.ts is unchanged.

evidence.why: docs/10 Project CI.md still says required jobs must be `success`, so the code and spec now disagree. No test covers a skipped required job.

checked.risk: Spec conformance (merge gate and job conclusion semantics)
Failure paths / guards fail closed (where skipped comes from)
Security: merge permission granted on non-success results
Real contracts, idempotency/state, build/runtime env: not applicable. This is a pure predicate change in a read-only gate, with no external calls, no state writes and no image changes.
